basics.name: Hang Yu
basics.label: Ph.D. Candidate in Computer Science (Human-Robot Interaction & Robot Learning), Tufts University
basics.summary: Hang Yu is a Ph.D. candidate in Computer Science at Tufts University, advised by Dr. Elaine Schaertl Short in the Assistive Agent and Behavior Learning (AABL) lab. Research on Human-Robot Interaction, robot learning from human feedback and demonstrations, Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, and agentic robotics, with open-sourced datasets collected in public spaces from real-world, non-expert users. Currently a Research Intern at ABB Robotics working on VLA models for bimanual manipulation.

work.name: ABB Robotics
work.summary: Building new Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for bimanual manipulation and exploring agentic robotics for industrial robotics. (Present)

work.name: Assistive Agent and Behavior Learning Lab (AABL), Tufts University
work.summary: Advised by Dr. Elaine Schaertl Short. Improving robot learning from multi-modular human teaching: human feedback, human demonstrations, and outputs from VLMs/LLMs. Most data is open-sourced and collected in public spaces from real-world, non-expert users.

work.summary: Teaching assistant for computer science courses.
